articles.title: Cabinet clears bills to raise 50% Lok Sabha seats across states, freeze delimitation till 2051
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid growing support for the delimitation bills with support of DMK, the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction and YSRCP, the Union Cabinet cleared the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid growing support for the delimitation bills with support of DMK, the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction and YSRCP, the Union Cabinet cleared the legislation to increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength from 550 to 850 by proposing a uniform increase of 50% in constituencies in every state, while freezing any fresh delimitation to revise the numbers till 2051.Government circulated the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill for delimitation and operationalisation of women’s quota from 2029, and another bill for setting up a Delimitation Commission to MPs on Friday as numbers appeared to be falling in place for Parliament’s nod to the government’s centrepiece legislation, only months after a united opposition had voted down the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill with similar objectives.A third bill will seek to facilitate an increase in the number of seats in the UTs of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry which have assemblies.“The objective of the present bill (Constitution amendment) is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in Lok Sabha and legislative assemblies of states and Union Territories, through a delimitation exercise. Such delimitation shall provide for an increase of 50% in the number of seats in Lok Sabha and assemblies of states and Union Territories over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation,” the Constitution amendment bill said.The new bill is different from its previous version in making an explicit constitutional provision to assuage the concerns of parties like DMK and NCP (SP) of any diminishment of the existing share of states in LS, opening the path for them to junk their past opposition and join the BJP-led NDA in backing the Constitution amendment bill that needs support of two-thirds MPs for passage.For the simultaneous pursuit of the two objectives, the bills have been predicated on the numbers of two Census exercises. For determining the respective share of states in LS, the 1971 Census -- the one which was used for determining the current share of states in LS, is being retained. However, for redrawing the boundaries of LS constituencies in states, the 2011 Census numbers will be used: something which frees the government of the need to wait for the findings of the enumeration currently underway.In the proposed maximum strength of 850 in Lok Sabha, 815 will be for states and 35 for UTs with assemblies -- Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir. The real overall strength of Lok Sabha is likely to be around 816. LS currently has a strength of 543 against the maximum possible strength of 550.The government is set to table the bills, key for implementation of women’s quota, in Lok Sabha on Nov 30. The bills are more granular in their legal casing as well as political outreach, while keeping the same broad agenda of rolling out one-third reservation for women in LS and state assemblies from 2029, when the next national election is due.Signalling his likely change of stand, DMK chief M K Stalin said the share of Tamil Nadu, which has 39 LS seats, should not fall below its current 7.18%, and the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years. The government had offered to meet the condition in April itself and the new bill addresses both of Stalin’s points.NCP(SP) was more categorical, with its senior functionary Jitendra Awhad quoting party boss Sharad Pawar to say that the party, an INDIA bloc constituent, had decided to support delimitation.DMK’s 22 MPs in LS, NCP (SP)’s eight and four of YSR Congress, which is also expected to support, takes NDA’s strength in the House to 355. With 360 needed for the bills’ passage in the House, which has three vacancies, NDA appears all but certain to cross the threshold amid indications from the governing alliance that some more MPs may either abstain or even back it.Attention is also focused on whether the speaker will give his ruling on the legality of the split in TMC which has resulted in 20 MPs belonging to Mamata Banerjee’s party aligning themselves with NDA. A favourable ruling will free them from any legal encumbrance in taking an independent course.The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, which will amend eight Articles of the Constitution, also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state assembly from 500 to 650. It is being explicitly done for Uttar Pradesh as its assembly, the largest in the country, currently has 403 members.Passage of the bill will also provide the government an effective plank to showcase its pro-women credentials in the run-up to a crucial round of state elections, and government is likely to build political capital out of it by getting endorsement from assemblies of states where BJP and its allies are in office.With a new delimitation bill being tabled, government will withdraw the earlier legislation which is still pending in Lok Sabha.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A North Dakota landowner said a 1993 property map gave him access over neighbours' land, but the deed and map were both recorded at noon; in 2026, the state Supreme Court rejected his easement claim
articles.summary: A North Dakota landowner who claimed that a 1993 subdivision map gave him the right to use access roads across his neighbours' properties lost his legal
articles.body: A North Dakota landowner who claimed that a 1993 subdivision map gave him the right to use access roads across his neighbours' properties lost his legal battle after the state Supreme Court found that he had failed to establish an easement. The dispute centred on two documents recorded at noon on the same day: a property map showing access easements and a deed transferring the middle parcel to a new owner. However, the court found that the landowner could not prove the deed had been delivered before the map was recorded.In its November 25, 2026 decision in Tamm v. Gatzke, available on Justia, the North Dakota Supreme Court also rejected claims that the access rights arose through long-term use or necessity. It affirmed the lower court's judgment denying Rudra Tamm's request to establish access across his neighbours' land.Dispute began with a 1993 property subdivisionAccording to the court's decision, F.M. Roberts owned a large property along River Road in Burleigh County in 1993. He subsequently divided it into three parcels known as Tracts 1-B, 2-B and 3-B. A subdivision map executed by Roberts on May 10, 1993, showed two strips marked as access easements. One crossed Tract 1-B and the other crossed Tract 3-B, with Tract 2-B situated between them.On the same day, Roberts transferred Tract 2-B to Scott Johnson through a warranty deed. Neither document mentioned a specific time of execution or delivery, but both were stamped as recorded at noon on May 10, 1993. The deed did not expressly mention any access easement.Over the years, ownership of the surrounding properties changed. Diane Gatzke eventually acquired Tract 1-B, while the Eggers family acquired Tract 3-B. Johnson transferred Tract 2-B to Tamm in 2010. In 2024, Tamm filed a lawsuit seeking a declaration that the access easements shown on the 1993 map benefited his property.Court examines whether map created an easementThe central question was whether Roberts still owned all three parcels when the subdivision map was recorded. Under North Dakota law, an owner cannot create an easement over land that the same person still owns. To establish an easement benefiting Tract 2-B, Tamm needed to prove that Roberts had already transferred that parcel to Johnson before recording the map.Tamm argued that Roberts delivered the deed to Johnson before noon on May 10, 1993. If that had happened, Roberts would have owned the surrounding parcels but not Tract 2-B when the map was recorded. However, Johnson was the only witness with personal knowledge of the transaction, and he could not clearly remember the sequence of events more than 30 years later.He testified that he assumed the deed exchange had taken place before he visited the recorder's office but acknowledged that he did not remember exactly when or how the documents were exchanged. The district court found that Tamm had failed to establish that the deed was delivered before the map was recorded. The Supreme Court agreed, explaining that the recording timestamps alone could not establish when ownership actually transferred because a deed takes effect upon delivery, not recording.Landowner also fails to prove implied access rightsTamm alternatively argued that the access easements had arisen through prior use of the property. An easement implied from pre-existing use can arise when land under common ownership is divided and one portion has historically been used to benefit another. However, the claimant must establish apparent, permanent and continuous use, along with other legal requirements.Tamm argued that a two-track road had existed since the 1960s and ran across the surrounding properties. The court found that the evidence did not clearly establish that Roberts had continuously used the disputed strips specifically to access Tract 2-B. Although witnesses described travelling along the road to reach equipment and other areas, that did not prove the required use for the middle parcel. The court therefore upheld the finding that Tamm had failed to establish an easement based on prior use.Court rejects easement by necessityTamm also argued that access across his neighbours' properties was necessary because the terrain along River Road made it difficult to construct a driveway. However, the court noted that Tract 2-B directly adjoined River Road. A former county engineer testified that access could potentially be created through openings in the property's non-access line, particularly through a less steep southern opening.Tamm had made informal enquiries about obtaining access but had not formally applied for an approach permit. The court concluded that he had not provided clear and convincing evidence that reasonable alternative access was unavailable.Supreme Court upholds neighbours' positionOn November 25, 2026, the North Dakota Supreme Court affirmed the district court's judgment, rejecting all three grounds for establishing an easement.The ruling means Tamm cannot claim a right to use the disputed access strips on the basis of the 1993 map, historical use or necessity. The decision leaves the neighbours' properties free from the easement claims asserted in the lawsuit.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Virginia construction worker fell about 20 feet while installing siding and later needed spinal surgery; seven years on, an appeals court has rejected his employer's bid to stop disability benefits
articles.summary: A Virginia appeals court has upheld ongoing temporary total disability benefits for construction worker Olegario Felipe Valles, who fell roughly 20 feet
articles.body: A Virginia appeals court has upheld ongoing temporary total disability benefits for construction worker Olegario Felipe Valles, who fell roughly 20 feet while installing siding in 2019 and underwent spinal fusion surgery. The Court of Appeals of Virginia on Nov. 24, 2026, issued its unpublished decision rejecting American Building Dynamics, Inc. and its insurer’s attempt to terminate the benefits, according to details on Justia U.S. Law.The ruling matters because it affirms that an injured worker does not lose disability protection simply because years have passed or because the employer argues that the worker can do some kind of work. The court found no error in the Virginia Workers’ Compensation Commission’s conclusion that Valles remained unable to perform his pre-injury job and had not shown he was capable of suitable alternative work.How the injury happenedValles was working for American Building Dynamics on June 20, 2019, when he fell approximately 20 feet while performing siding work. The fall caused serious injuries and led to surgeries and continuing medical treatment. The Workers’ Compensation Commission later awarded him temporary total disability benefits and lifetime medical benefits for the consequences of the workplace accident.In January 2022, Valles underwent lumbar fusion surgery, a major spinal procedure intended to stabilize part of the lower back. Even after the operation, his treating physician, Dr. Zafar, noted that Valles continued to struggle with symptoms and functional limitations. The case therefore moved beyond the immediate aftermath of the fall and into the long-term question of whether he could return to meaningful work.The employer and insurer eventually filed an application to terminate Valles’s temporary total disability payments. Their position was that he had reached maximum medical improvement and could perform work within his physical restrictions. The Commission disagreed, finding that the employer had not met its burden to prove that suitable work was available to him.What the employer arguedAmerican Building Dynamics and its insurer asked the Court of Appeals to overturn the Commission’s decision. They argued that Valles could perform light-duty work and that the Commission had wrongly continued benefits despite evidence that he was capable of some employment. The appeal focused on whether the Commission’s factual findings and legal conclusions were supported by the record.The company relied on the idea that Valles’s condition had improved enough after surgery to allow work within restrictions. But the court found that the evidence did not establish that he could perform his former construction job, nor that the employer had made a genuine offer of suitable alternative employment that he could physically perform.Virginia workers’ compensation law places the burden on an employer seeking to end temporary total disability benefits to show that the employee is able to return to work. That usually means identifying work that fits the employee’s physical limitations and showing that the job is actually available. A general assertion that light-duty work exists is not enough.Why the court affirmedThe Court of Appeals reviewed the Commission’s findings under a deferential standard. It does not reweigh evidence as though it were hearing the case for the first time. Instead, it asks whether the Commission’s decision was supported by credible evidence and whether it made an error of law. The court concluded that the Commission’s denial of the termination application was supported by the record.The court noted that Valles continued to have significant limitations after lumbar fusion surgery. Dr. Zafar’s observations about his ongoing difficulties supported the Commission’s conclusion that he had not recovered sufficiently to resume his prior work. The appellate court also found no basis to disturb the Commission’s assessment of the medical and vocational evidence.The decision does not say that Valles will receive benefits forever without further review. Temporary total disability benefits can be changed if his condition improves, if he returns to work, or if the employer later proves that suitable work is available. But as of this ruling, the employer had not carried that burden.Seven years after the fallThe length of the case is striking. Valles fell in 2019, had spinal fusion surgery in 2022, and was still litigating the continuation of benefits in 2026. That timeline reflects the reality that serious workplace injuries can create years of medical treatment, rehabilitation, disputes over work capacity, and appeals.For injured workers, the case shows why medical documentation matters. Reports from treating physicians, evidence of continuing symptoms, restrictions on lifting, bending, standing, or climbing, and testimony about the physical demands of the old job can all affect whether benefits continue. The court’s decision rested on the Commission’s evaluation of that evidence, not on a simple assumption that surgery should have restored the worker to full capacity.For employers, the decision is a reminder that terminating benefits requires proof, not merely an argument that a worker should be able to return to some job. The employer must establish both the worker’s ability to perform a particular job and the availability of that job. Without that connection, a request to end benefits is likely to fail.What it means for workersThe ruling is a practical win for Valles because it preserves income support while he remains unable to work in his former role. It also reinforces an important protection in Virginia’s workers’ compensation system: an injured employee is not expected to prove that no job anywhere exists. The employer bears the burden when it seeks to cut off benefits.The case is also a reminder that back injuries can have lasting effects even after major surgery. A fall from height can cause damage that does not resolve cleanly, and spinal fusion may reduce pain or stabilize the spine without restoring the physical capacity needed for demanding construction work. The court’s decision recognized that reality by leaving the Commission’s findings intact.Seven years after the fall, Valles’s benefits remain in place. The employer’s appeal failed, and the Court of Appeals affirmed the Commission’s decision to continue temporary total disability payments.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A 14-year-old Iranian girl was beaten to death by her husband 10 days after giving birth; she was forced into marriage at 13, while another pregnant woman, 21, was shot dead the same day
articles.summary: A 14-year-old Iranian girl was allegedly beaten to death by her husband just 10 days after giving birth, after asking him if she could visit her family.
articles.body: A 14-year-old Iranian girl was allegedly beaten to death by her husband just 10 days after giving birth, after asking him if she could visit her family. The teenager, Sogand Moshtareki, had reportedly been forced into marriage at the age of 13. Her husband, who is 20, confessed to the killing and cited "family disputes" as the motive, according to the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI)'s Women Committee.Sogand, from Kerman province, was killed on November 6. Her death came on the same day as the murder of another young woman, 21-year-old Sepideh Raeisi, who was four months pregnant and was reportedly shot by her husband after trying to pursue a divorce.The two cases have renewed concerns over child marriage, domestic violence and the risks faced by women and girls in Iran. Human rights groups and campaigners say that forced marriages and limited legal protections can leave young women particularly vulnerable to abuse.Husband allegedly restricted Sogand's contact with her familyAccording to Iran Human Rights (IHR), information provided by Sogand's father indicated that her husband had restricted her contact with her family. He would reportedly lock her inside the house when he went out.Sogand had also recently survived a traffic accident and was still recovering when she gave birth. Her husband is understood to have been arrested, IHR said.The NCRI's Women Committee said the teenager had asked her husband for permission to visit her family shortly before she was killed. The organisation reported that he confessed to the murder and described the motive as "family disputes".Another young woman killed while pregnant on the same daySogand's death was reported on the same day as the killing of Sepideh Raeisi, a 21-year-old woman from Fars province. Sepideh, who had a three-year-old child and was four months pregnant, was shot by her husband after attempting to seek a divorce, according to the source material.Her unborn child did not survive, and her mother was injured in the incident.The NCRI said Sepideh had also been forced into marriage at the age of 13 and had endured years of domestic abuse. The cases have drawn attention to the dangers faced by girls who are married as children and later experience violence within their marriages.Campaigners warn of the risks of child marriage in IranThe NCRI says girls forced into marriage are denied opportunities for education, personal development and free choice. It has also warned that child marriage can expose girls to domestic violence, early pregnancy and economic dependency, with some cases ending in lethal violence.The organisation reported 24 cases of femicide in Iran in October 2026 alone. Most of the victims were reportedly killed in their homes by men known to them. The NCRI cautioned that the actual number could be higher because many cases go unreported.Separately, UK-based Persian-language broadcaster Iran International reported that at least 84 women and girls were killed in Iran between March 21 and October 13. In 75 of those cases, the alleged perpetrators were known to the victims. Eight of the underage girls were reportedly killed by their fathers, brothers or other male relatives.According to the Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights, at least 207 femicides were recorded across Iran in 2025, including 31 cases involving suspected so-called "honour" motives. The organisation said at least 13 women were killed after rejecting marriage proposals, ten after seeking divorce and ten in cases linked to child marriage.Other recent cases raise further concernsSeveral other reported killings have brought renewed attention to violence against women and girls in Iran.In a separate case, 19-year-old Helia Fattahi, who was two months pregnant, was allegedly killed by her parents in what Hengaw described as a so-called honour killing. The organisation said her parents, Voria Fattahi and Leila Veisi, allegedly forced her to take around 30 anticonvulsant pills and beat her before suffocating her with a pillow.Hengaw said the parents confessed to the killing when emergency medical personnel arrived. Police later arrested them in Sanandaj, in western Iran. Police said the parents had cited "family disputes" as the motive.On November 18, 23-year-old Sadaf Haghbin was shot dead at her birthday party in Gilan province. Local media reported that a former boyfriend was responsible for the shooting, while the Khabaronline news site said the suspected motive was her refusal to marry him.Another case involved 16-year-old Sogand Sayyadi, whose body was found in the courtyard of her residential building in Kermanshah on November 15. According to Hengaw, the teenager had warned her school that she feared her father might hurt or kill her if she went home with him.The organisation alleged that her father, Kioumars Sayyadi, assaulted her in front of classmates and school staff before continuing the attack outside the school. Hengaw, citing sources, said he killed her the following day by throwing her from the fifth floor of the family's apartment building.The judiciary-affiliated Mizan news agency reported that her father was detained on suspicion of assault and murder. The school principal was also arrested on suspicion of negligence, citing provincial chief prosecutor Hamidreza Karimi.What does Iranian law say about so-called honour killings?Iran's Islamic Penal Code does not specifically criminalise so-called honour killings, according to a UK Home Office report on women facing honour-based violence in the country. Article 301 exempts fathers and paternal grandfathers who kill their children or grandchildren from qisas, or retribution in kind, which can otherwise result in the death penalty.Under Article 612 of Iran's Penal Code, a person whose murder conviction does not result in qisas may face three to ten years in prison if the court determines that the killing has disturbed public order or could encourage further offences. Amnesty International has also raised concerns about how these legal provisions can facilitate impunity in so-called honour killings.Estimates of honour killings in Iran vary. The US State Department has cited figures ranging from 375 to 450 such killings annually, while the UK Home Office report refers to estimates of at least 450 cases a year. The actual number is difficult to establish because reliable official statistics are not available.Human rights organisations have criticised these legal provisions, arguing that exemptions from qisas and comparatively lighter sentences can weaken accountability and leave women and girls inadequately protected.You use AI every day. articles.title: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday. Addressing the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), an inter-governmental body comprising 23 member-states, he said international law, particularly United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected.The 25th meeting of the IORA council of ministers here was followed by a joint communique that expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.PM Narendra Modi met the foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 IORA member-states participating in the meeting. “Indian Ocean has connected our people for a millennia. As chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of Mahasagar (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region,” he posted on X.According to the Delhi communique, IORA reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law to ensure “freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the sea”. It also reaffirmed its commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence and mutual benefit.India announced a grant of $500,000 for the association’s institutional and financial capacity-building. “Whether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners,” said Jaishankar.“We are focused on the volatile aspects of a transforming global order, especially conflicts, frictions and disruptions. It is equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects: deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation,” he said.The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and of shared challenges, he stressed. “Our collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development,” Jaishankar added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The opposition Friday was staring at possible passage of the delimitation bill, after DMK and NCP (SP), which were critical to its defeat in April, signalled willingness to back the legislation. Congress said BJP wants to “change the Constitution” through delimitation after the ruling party failed to achieve it with the “400 paar” election, alleging the redrawing of LS seats would be done by “compromised” CEC Gyanesh Kumar, who has been “exposed” for manipulating electoral rolls.Vowing to “expose” BJP, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal said, “Modi and Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this episode.” But the mood in the opposition was despondent as its persisting confidence about unity in the anti-bill ranks dissipated with statements from M K Stalin and NCP (SP) leaders.There was regret within that the Congress’s decision to abruptly dump a staunch ally, the DMK, in favour of TVK to form govt in TN had angered the Dravidian party into drifting towards BJP. The attacks from Congress leaders on DMK on Friday reflected the anger at the former ally, even as TN Congress members were peppered with queries about whether they regretted leaving the DMK alliance.Odisha’s interests to guide party’s delimitation stand: BJDAhead of the special sitting of Parliament, BJD Friday said party president Naveen Patnaik will take the final call on delimitation and the women’s reservation bills, with Odisha’s interests guiding the party’s stand, reports Ashok Pradhan. “Our decision will be guided by Odisha’s interests. articles.title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of complicity in the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi and brought down the United Front government in 1998, then anything can happen in politics. Thus said a multi-term DMK MP over the prospect of his party’s widely-expected support to BJP in securing passage of the delimitation bill in Parliament after it was in the vanguard of opposition to the governing party since 2014.While DMK’s support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment and offer the national party a fresh opening in Tamil Nadu, which has remained a tough nut for it to crack despite repeated attempts. It certainly weakens the anti-South charge DMK, Congress and others have levelled against BJP.Besides making explicit provision in the bill that the share of every state in Lok Sabha will remain the same and the maximum strength of LS will be frozen till 2051, both concessions aimed at winning over DMK, BJP has of late made subtle moves to dial down its push for legislative measures which had drawn sharp opposition from the Tamil party.This includes a sudden slowdown in the working of two parliamentary committees overseeing Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which has proposed an apex regulator in place of several for higher education, and a Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of PM, CMs and ministers detained on criminal charges for 30 continuous days, when they were on the verge of adopting their reports.DMK, which has long championed state autonomy and decried central government’s alleged encroachment on its turf, has been sharply critical of both bills.Both parties have a history of working together. BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. Their “secular” opposition to BJP, which then moved closer to DMK’s rival AIADMK, helped them explain away their alliance. DMK’s current challenge is the sudden emergence of Vijay-led TVK as Congress dumped it overnight to help the star actor become chief minister.With DMK out of INDIA bloc, its options are limited. With misgivings persisting in a section of party over joining hands with BJP, which too has been a bitter critic of its anti-Hindutva rhetoric, political compulsions may be the glue for them in the same it worked for DMK and Congress in 2004.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: BJP started talks with DMK even before 2026 elections
articles.summary: DMK to back BJP’s delimitation bill after year-long talks, citing safeguards: proportional seat rise for Tamil Nadu and extending the 1971 census freeze.
articles.body: CHENNAI: When DMK’s 22 Lok Sabha members vote in favour of the BJP-led Union governement’s delimitation bill, it would mark the end of a series of discussions the two parties had had over more than a year.All through, DMK stood by its two demands: Proportional increase of seats for Tamil Nadu and freezing the 1971 census as the basis for another 25 years. The party has convened a meeting of its 22 Lok Sabha members and eight Rajya Sabha members on Saturday to endorse the decision.DMK parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi Rajathi Karunanidhi has been the prime negotiator with BJP, even before the 2026 assembly election. BJP was in touch with DMK even before the bill was first introduced in April, sources said. “The bill was defeated then because of DMK. The present arrangement is also because of DMK. The leadership placed the two demands before BJP when the latter reached out,” a senior DMK leader said. “The latest bill is a fair deal. It will be beneficial for both DMK as well as Tamil Nadu.”BJP’s argument was that if the bill was defeated, a new census process would kick in and the relevant constitutional provisions would come into force next year.For months, DMK’s opposition to delimitation was rooted in a “clear fear” that Tamil Nadu would lose 10 seats. Stalin had burnt the draft delimitation bill in April, calling it a “black law”. The party said if Lok Sabha seats were redistributed based on the 2027 census, states such as Tamil Nadu, which had successfully controlled population growth, could lose representation. It had warned that Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18% share of Lok Sabha seats could be diluted and had sought a 25-year extension of the freeze based on the 1971 census.In fact, Stalin had even sought to build a wider political consensus on the issue by convening a meeting of chief ministers in March 2025. The meeting passed a resolution calling for fair delimitation. DMK now argues that its earlier resistance forced the BJP-led governement to offer safeguards, enabling the party to convert its opposition into a political gain.The party has lost allies to TVK and quit the INDIA bloc, leaving it vulnerable to criticism from Congress and other erstwhile allies. “Just because Congress is worried, we cannot go against Tamil Nadu’s interests. Had we not opposed the bill in the past, we could have lost this proposition. Since BJP is ready to incorporate these two demands, we have nothing to lose but to gain more in future,” another DMK leader said.DMK backed a resolution passed by the TVK governement in the Assembly in Aug, urging the Centre to retain the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.In a post on X, Stalin said DMK would never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests, nor would it depart from its principles. “DMK stands firm on these two demands and will continue to do so. articles.title: 2,200 shipping containers once stacked into an Arizona border wall may find a second life as rental homes: a Tucson nonprofit wants to convert 350 to 450 steel boxes into affordable housing but is still raising funds
articles.summary: Steel boxes once stacked along the US-Mexico border to keep migrants out could soon be turned into homes for people struggling to afford rent.
articles.body: Steel boxes once stacked along the US-Mexico border to keep migrants out could soon be turned into homes for people struggling to afford rent. A Tucson nonprofit, Boxes of Hope, is working with affordable housing developer La Frontera to convert 350 to 450 of the containers into rental homes, according to Realtor.com.The proposed village would give a second life to shipping containers left behind after Arizona dismantled its controversial border barrier. The project is still in the planning and fundraising stage, but its organisers have identified a potential site and are working towards securing the land. “These were built to keep people out, and now we're welcoming people in,” Boxes of Hope founder Beau Phillips told Realtor.com, describing the idea as one with “poetic justice”.The containers were part of a makeshift border barrier installed under former Arizona governor Doug Ducey in 2022. More than 2,000 double-stacked steel shipping containers were placed near Yuma and in the Coronado National Forest, with wire added on top.The barrier faced legal challenges from the federal government and environmental groups, which argued that it had been placed illegally on federal and tribal land. Arizona began dismantling it in early 2023, leaving about 2,200 steel containers without a clear future, Realtor.com reported.Phillips, a semiretired marketing executive, came across the containers while flying over the Arizona desert in 2023. The sight prompted him to approach state officials about buying the surplus boxes and repurposing them for housing. He subsequently founded Boxes of Hope and partnered with La Frontera, a Tucson-based community behavioural healthcare provider and affordable housing developer. The project also brings in container-conversion expert Ryan Egan, who is expected to oversee construction.The proposed village is planned for Southeast Tucson, on a 25- to 30-acre site within about two miles of where the containers are currently stored. Organisers are looking for land with access to utilities, public transport and essential services, including grocery stores. The exact location has not yet been disclosed. Boxes of Hope hopes to reveal the village's name, location and development plan in January 2027, after finalising arrangements with the landowner.Each converted container is expected to provide about 300 square feet of living space. The homes would include a private bedroom with room for a queen-sized bed, a living area, kitchenette, full bathroom and storage. The units would also receive new flooring, walls and windows, along with dense insulation and mini-split air-conditioning systems designed to make them suitable for Arizona's hot summers. Sliding glass doors and other upgrades are part of the proposed design.The estimated conversion cost is about $59,000 per home, according to Realtor.com. Phillips said this would be roughly half the cost of what the city of Tucson pays private builders to construct affordable housing.The village is intended for a broad group of residents, including singles, couples, seniors, veterans, single parents, teachers and workers priced out of the local rental market. Tucson's median asking rent stood at $1,133 in October, according to Realtor.com.The project is also designed to provide support beyond housing. Plans include a community kitchen and dining hall, laundry facilities, a park, transitional housing for people experiencing homelessness, behavioural healthcare and job training in trades such as carpentry and plumbing.La Frontera CEO Dan Ranieri has emphasised that stable housing alone may not be enough to help residents rebuild their lives. The partnership aims to combine affordable homes with services that could help people gain skills, access care and move towards greater independence.The proposal comes as Tucson faces pressure on its affordable housing supply. More than 40,000 residents are reported to be waiting for housing assistance, a figure cited by the project and local reporting. Boxes of Hope has received support from Tucson city leadership, the Arizona Department of Housing and the office of US Senator Mark Kelly. However, the nonprofit is still seeking donations, private contributions and government housing grants to move the project from planning into construction.The organisation hopes to begin site development in spring 2027, with the first residents potentially moving in during the second half of the year. The schedule remains dependent on fundraising, land arrangements and the development process. Phillips believes the idea could eventually be replicated in other cities, particularly as large numbers of shipping containers arrive in the United States through imports.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Los Angeles mansion listed for $65 million in January 2026 has sold for $38.65 million; the 20,000-square-foot Brentwood estate was reportedly bought by Adam Adelson, son of late casino billionaire Sheldon Adelson
articles.summary: A newly built Brentwood mansion that entered the market in January 2026 with a $65 million asking price has sold for $38.65 million, according to
articles.body: A newly built Brentwood mansion that entered the market in January 2026 with a $65 million asking price has sold for $38.65 million, according to RealtyWire’s roundup of the Los Angeles Westside’s top home sales for the week ending November 22. The roughly 20,000-square-foot estate at 401 North Tigertail Road, known as Villa Serenique, was reportedly purchased by Adam Adelson, son of the late casino billionaire Sheldon Adelson.The sale represents a discount of $26.35 million, or about 41 percent, from the original January listing price. It is still one of the largest residential transactions reported in the Westside that week, leading RealtyWire’s Top 5 list ahead of a $21 million Beverly Hills penthouse and a $9.275 million Malibu home. Read more about it here:A major Brentwood new buildVilla Serenique is a contemporary estate of about 20,000 square feet on a 1.06-acre lot in Brentwood, minutes from Brentwood Village. The house was completed in 2026 after four years of construction and was designed with Tiffany Harris Design. It has nine bedrooms, 15 bathrooms, and three levels of living space.The property was wrapped inside and out in hand-chiseled Portuguese limestone, with Roman plaster, travertine, and board-formed concrete. Its design emphasizes glass walls, hillside views, and indoor-outdoor living, with the main entertaining level opening to lawns planted with olive and citrus trees.The listing describes a home built for large-scale entertaining as well as private living. It includes a chef’s kitchen with a brass hood, a separate industrial prep kitchen, two guest suites, a walnut-paneled office, and an open-air kitchen with both gas and Argentinian-style grills.What the buyer getsThe upper level contains the primary suite, which has a private balcony, custom walk-in closets, and two bathrooms with heated floors and silver travertine details. Three additional bedroom suites and a lounge share that floor. The lower level is devoted to wellness and entertainment, with a soundproof theater, wine cellar, bar, lap pool, steam spa, infrared sauna, cold plunge, Pilates studio, and a gym that opens outdoors.There is also a car gallery that can function as a drive-in movie space, along with garage capacity for 10 cars. Outside, the property includes gardens, an Italian-style dining terrace, a pickleball court, and a soccer field.Realtor.com’s listing history shows that the land sold for $6.85 million in 2021, before the current house was built. The home was first listed in January 2026 for $65 million, then relisted in April at $54 million before ultimately selling for $38.65 million.Why the price fellA reduction of more than $26 million is unusually large, even in Los Angeles’s ultra-luxury market. It suggests that the initial $65 million valuation did not attract a buyer at that level, and that the seller or developers eventually adjusted the price to meet the market. The property’s listing history shows it was removed from the market in April after 88 days at the original price, then returned at $54 million.The final sale price works out to roughly $1,933 per square foot for a 20,000-square-foot home. That remains an exceptionally high price by ordinary standards, but it is far below the $3,250 per square foot implied by the original $65 million listing.Luxury homes often carry ambitious asking prices because they are unique, newly built, and difficult to compare with nearby sales. But buyers at this level have choices, and a home’s design, location, operating costs, and resale prospects all affect what they will pay. Villa Serenique’s eventual sale price indicates that the market placed a more conservative value on the property than its opening price suggested.Who reportedly bought itRealtyWire reports that the buyer was represented by Chad Rogers of Hilton & Hyland and identifies the purchaser as Adam Adelson, son of the late Sheldon Adelson, the casino billionaire and Republican political donor. The report does not provide a public statement from the buyer or confirm the transaction through a separate official filing.The listing agent was Santiago Arana of The Agency. RealtyWire notes that Arana represented the seller in the Brentwood transaction, while Rogers represented the buyer.If the reported buyer is confirmed, the purchase would add another high-profile name to Brentwood’s roster of luxury homeowners. The neighborhood has long attracted entertainment, technology, finance, and business figures because of its privacy, hillside setting, and proximity to both Los Angeles and the Westside’s business and cultural centers.What it says about the marketThe sale is a useful data point for anyone watching Los Angeles’s high-end housing market. It shows that even a newly completed, highly specified estate can sell well below its initial asking price when the market does not support the number. The property still commanded $38.65 million, but the gap between the opening and closing prices was substantial.It also illustrates how pricing strategy can shape a sale. The home’s first price may have been intended to establish a premium position, but the eventual transaction suggests that the seller needed to move closer to what buyers were willing to pay. In a market where a small number of buyers can afford homes above $30 million, even minor differences in perceived value can have major consequences.For now, Villa Serenique has changed hands at $38.65 million, making it the top reported Westside sale of the week. The deal is a reminder that in luxury real estate, an asking price is only a starting point, and the final number is set by what a buyer is ultimately willing to pay.You use AI every day. articles.title: AP seeks 90% central funding for ₹4,851 crore cyclone-resilient power infrastructure
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh seeks 90% central funding for ₹4,851 crore cyclone-resilient power project, including underground cabling and spun poles in coastal areas.
articles.body: Vijayawada: The state govt has sought 90% financial assistance from the Centre for a proposed ₹4,851 crore project to develop cyclone-resilient power infrastructure in coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh, with a focus on underground cabling and the use of spun poles to strengthen electricity distribution networks.Energy minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar, who is on a visit to New Delhi, raised the proposal during a meeting with Union power minister Manohar Lal Khattar on the sidelines of a conference of state power ministers organised by the Centre.Gottipati explained how recent cyclones had severely damaged the state’s power infrastructure, particularly in coastal districts, resulting in extensive damage to electricity poles, transmission and distribution lines and other assets. He stressed the need to develop a robust power network capable of withstanding extreme weather events and reducing disruptions during natural calamities.In a letter submitted to Khattar, Gottipati requested the Centre to bear 90% of the estimated project cost of ₹4,851 crore, stating that the proposed works would significantly improve the resilience of the power distribution system in vulnerable coastal areas. The state govt has also outlined an implementation plan under which the project could be completed within three years if the Centre extends the required financial support. The proposed infrastructure includes underground power cables and reconstruction of vulnerable overhead lines using spun poles designed to withstand strong winds and severe weather conditions.Gottipati said the proposed cyclone-resilient network would help minimise damage to electricity infrastructure during disasters and enable power utilities to restore supply quickly. It would also reduce asset losses and technical losses while ensuring greater reliability of electricity supply to households, industries and essential services.The minister explained that investing in resilient infrastructure would be more cost-effective in the long run than repeatedly rebuilding damaged power networks after every cyclone. articles.title: Widowed woman raises 3 children in matrimonial home for over 25 years after husband's death; Delhi HC says father-in-law cannot evict her until he provides alternative accommodation or pays Rs 25,000 monthly rent
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A widowed woman who has lived in her matrimonial home for more than 25 years cannot be forced to leave it until her father-in-law arranges
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A widowed woman who has lived in her matrimonial home for more than 25 years cannot be forced to leave it until her father-in-law arranges another place for her to stay or pays her Rs 25,000 a month towards rent, the Delhi High Court has ruled. The court has upheld the father's claim to ownership of the house, but said the possession order in his favour would remain unenforceable until the woman's housing needs were addressed.While deciding the woman's appeal against a 2024 trial court decree, the high court said the law had to balance the property owner's right to recover his home with the widow's entitlement to residence under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. The woman married on September 11, 2000, and moved into the house with her husband. The couple raised their three children there. After her husband died on May 1, 2016, she continued to live in the property.Her father-in-law, who said the house belonged exclusively to him under a sale deed executed on January 19, 2001, revoked the family's permission to stay through a legal notice in December 2016. His two other sons left the house, but the widow remained. He subsequently filed a suit seeking possession of the ground floor and Rs 25,000 a month in damages for its occupation. The trial court granted him possession in April 2024, but refused damages as he had not provided evidence to establish the amount.The woman appealed, contending that the property was ancestral and that she had a right to remain there as it was her shared household. The high court found no evidence linking ancestral funds to the purchase of the property and rejected her claim on that ground. The sale deed was in her father-in-law's name.However, the court said the ownership documents did not settle the question of her right to residence. Having lived in the house with her husband for nearly 16 years and brought up their children there, the property was their established family home. Under Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act, a woman's right to reside in a shared household does not depend on whether she owns it. The court said the right was not extinguished by her husband's death or by the father-in-law withdrawing permission for her to stay.It also allowed her to rely on this protection in the appeal, despite not having expressly described the house as a shared household in her written statement. The relevant facts had been pleaded and were not disputed. The court further examined the widow's entitlement to maintenance under Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. The provision requires a father-in-law to maintain a widowed daughter-in-law who cannot support herself from her own earnings, property or other specified sources. Such maintenance, the court said, includes a place to live.The woman had studied up to Class 10. The court found no evidence that she had an independent income, property or an estate left by her husband. Her father-in-law pointed to Rs 25.13 lakh she had received in 2016 through execution proceedings arising from an arbitration award in her late husband's favour. The high court clarified that the amount was not Rs 1 crore and did not constitute insurance money.The court said the sum had been received nearly 10 years earlier to support four family members and could not reasonably be expected to fund the woman's housing for the rest of her life. Although the amount was relevant while deciding what the father-in-law should provide, it did not mean she no longer needed shelter. The judge also noted that the relationship between the two had broken down, making it unsuitable for them to continue living together.The possession decree was therefore upheld, but its execution was made conditional. The father-in-law must either provide the woman with suitable alternative accommodation comparable to her existing home or pay Rs 25,000 every month so that she can rent a similar place. The court said the monthly amount was based on the valuation the father-in-law himself had placed on the ground-floor occupation in his suit. It also made clear that the order would not determine either side's claims in the pending partition case, which must be decided separately.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: IndiGo lifts partial Saudi flight curbs but keeps Riyadh, Dammam services grounded
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: IndiGo has resumed select flight operations to and from Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah and Madinah, while extending the suspension of services to Riyadh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: IndiGo has resumed select flight operations to and from Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah and Madinah, while extending the suspension of services to Riyadh and Dammam until December 7, 2026, amid continuing security concerns in the region.In a travel advisory posted on X on Friday, November 28, the airline said the decision followed an assessment of the prevailing situation and operational requirements.“Following a careful assessment of the prevailing situation and the associated operational considerations, we are pleased to resume select flight operations to and from Jeddah and Madinah. However, flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain cancelled until 7 December 2026 (inclusive),” IndiGo said.The airline said passengers affected by the cancellations were being informed through their registered contact details. It also advised travellers to check their flight status through its website or mobile application before proceeding to the airport.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh subsequently shared the airline’s update on X, confirming the partial resumption of services and the continued suspension of flights to the Saudi capital and Dammam.“Indigo airlines announces resumption of select flight operations to and from Jeddah and Madinah. However, flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain cancelled until 7 December 2026,” the embassy wrote.The latest announcement marks a partial revision of IndiGo’s November 18 advisory, when the airline had cancelled all flights connecting Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam until November 30, citing the prevailing security situation in Saudi Arabia.At the time, IndiGo said, “In view of the prevailing security situation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam have been cancelled until 30 November 2026 (inclusive).”The flight disruptions come against the backdrop of renewed Houthi attacks targeting Saudi infrastructure. A strike on an oil refinery in the kingdom’s Jazan region on Thursday killed one person.Al Jazeera reported that the Arab League condemned what it described as the “repeated terrorist attacks launched by the Houthi militia” against Saudi Arabia.“Targeting oil facilities and vital economic infrastructure constitutes a flagrant violation of the kingdom’s sovereignty,” the organisation said.Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi described the attack as a “dangerous escalation”, while Qatar called it a “reprehensible act of aggression” and a “clear breach” of international law, Al Jazeera reported.Travellers with bookings to Saudi Arabia have been advised to verify flight schedules before departure, with services to Riyadh and Dammam remaining suspended through December 7.

articles.title: Deepam lighting at Deepathoon today: CRPF deployed in TN's Thiruparankundram after SC order
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has been deployed in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram to oversee security and surveillance on Saturday
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has been deployed in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram to oversee security and surveillance on Saturday after the Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop the hill.The deployment comes amid a dispute over compliance with the court's earlier order allowing the lamp to be lit at the site.A senior CRPF officer said one company of the force has been stationed in the area and is awaiting further instructions from higher authorities."One Company of CRPF has been deployed. We will get directions from higher authorities," news agency ANI quoted the officer as saying.On Friday, the Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai on November 28. It also permitted devotees to participate in the ceremony and ordered the deployment of the CRPF to ensure its smooth conduct.The direction came amid a controversy over the non-lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon, despite an interim order of the Supreme Court permitting the ceremony at the site.The Maha Deepam was instead lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple as part of the annual Karthigai Deepam festival on Tuesday. Police personnel had been deployed near the Deepathoon ahead of the scheduled ceremony.The Supreme Court bench on Saturday found "wilful disobedience" of its earlier order, noting that the ceremonial lamp was not lit on November 24 despite the court's directions and an undertaking given by the Madurai district collector before the Madras HC to ensure compliance.A bench led by Justice Aravind Kumar had permitted a strictly conditional, one-time lighting of the lamp on November 24, while clarifying that the direction would neither set a legal precedent nor resolve broader claims concerning ownership and customary rights.On November 20, the Tamil Nadu government filed a review petition in the Supreme Court challenging its interim order permitting a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, located near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah on Thiruparankundram Hill.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: “Stopped to help an injured delivery agent, ended up delivering his orders": Bengaluru man's unexpected act of kindness turns into a heartwarming story of humanity that has won hearts online
articles.summary: Sometimes, an ordinary day can take an unexpected turn, leading to experiences one never plans for.
articles.body: Sometimes, an ordinary day can take an unexpected turn, leading to experiences one never plans for. For a Bengaluru man, what began as a casual walk back home from a friend's place turned into a hospital visit, a temporary food delivery job and an unexpected friendship with a stranger.The man recently shared his unusual experience on Reddit, explaining how he came across a food delivery worker who had met with an accident. Instead of simply walking past, he stopped to help the injured man and took him to a hospital. But his act of kindness did not end there.When he learnt that the delivery worker still had several food orders waiting to be delivered, he offered to complete them himself. Despite having absolutely no experience in food delivery, he took charge of the pending orders and figured out the process along the way. Sharing the incident on the r/BangaloreSocial subreddit, the man began his post with an amusing observation: "Went out for a walk and somehow ended up delivering food orders today."A routine walk turned into an unexpected rescueAccording to the Reddit post, the incident happened around 11:30 am when the man was returning home after visiting a friend. Recounting how everything unfolded, he wrote, "I was walking back home from a friend's place when I came across a delivery guy who had met with an accident. I stopped to help him and ended up taking him to the hospital." Thankfully, the delivery worker was doing okay after the accident. However, he had a few food orders that were still pending, leaving him with another problem to deal with.The Bengaluru man could have continued with his day after helping the injured worker reach the hospital. Instead, he decided to take things a step further and offered to complete the deliveries on his behalf. Explaining his spontaneous decision, he wrote, "Now, I don’t know what came over me, but I asked him if he wanted me to deliver them."With no delivery experience, he figured things out along the wayWhat happened next was something the man himself had not anticipated when he stepped out of his house. He agreed to take over the food orders despite having no previous experience working as a delivery agent. He had to understand the process as he went along, navigating the deliveries one by one. Describing his unexpected role, he wrote, "And that’s how I randomly became a delivery guy for a while today. Had absolutely no experience, just took the orders and figured things out along the way."Once he had completed all the pending deliveries, he did not simply part ways with the worker. He also offered to drop him home. The two ended up laughing about the unusual situation and spent some time talking about work, life and their everyday experiences. The man shared that the entire episode had been completely unplanned, but it gave him an opportunity to interact with someone whose daily working life he might otherwise never have experienced.Went out for a walk and somehow ended up delivering food orders today 😂 byu/BassOwn1919 inBangaloreSocialDelivery worker's monthly earnings caught him by surpriseDuring their conversation, the Bengaluru man also learnt something about the delivery worker's income that he had not expected. According to his post, the delivery worker mentioned that he earned around Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000 every month. The figure caught the man's attention and became another memorable part of their conversation. He did not share further details about the worker's working hours, delivery platform or how the monthly earnings were calculated.From a hospital visit to food deliveries, the day ended with a smileLooking back at the experience, the man described how dramatically his plans had changed within a few hours. He had left home expecting nothing more than an ordinary walk. Instead, he ended up helping an accident victim, visiting a hospital, delivering food orders and dropping a stranger home. Summing up the unexpected chain of events, he wrote, "The whole thing was so unexpected. I left home for a casual walk and somehow ended up at a hospital, delivering food orders and dropping a stranger home."He also ended his post with a simple wish for the delivery worker's recovery, writing, "Anyway, hope he’s doing well now." The post drew appreciative reactions from Reddit users, with several praising his willingness to help someone he had never met. One user commented, "Working people and youngsters in this city are so nice."Another simply reacted, "Woahhhh crazy." What makes this incident memorable is not just that a stranger took over someone's food deliveries without prior experience. It is also how one person's decision to stop and help turned into a series of thoughtful gestures. For the injured delivery worker, it meant receiving help when he needed it.
